newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close up a hair in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close up a hair in slow trade.

text.p: Caracas share prices closed up a hair in trade slowed by the onset of summer holidays and continuing stock market volatility in Brazil, traders said.
The bolsa's 19-share index ended up 0.2 percent at 9,121.60 points as 54 million shares traded, worth 5.3 billion bolivars ($11 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
"Summer holidays are approaching and that, combined with the problems in Brazil, brought a slow session and lower volume," Banesco broker Simon Brad said.
Brazilian stocks dropped in roller-coaster trade last week on devaluation fears that sent shock waves through the region.

Merinvest's composite index, which includes telephone company CANTV, meanwhile closed down 0.2 percent at 141.44 points. Among traded issues, 20 fell, 18 rose and seven closed flat -- including Corimon B shares, despite heavy turnover.
Shareholders at the paints and packaging company are due to decide this evening on plans to convert preferred B shares into A shares.
Brokers said the conversion would pave the way for resumption of ADR trading on the New York stock exchange, halted since January 1996.
